All wired and syntax-checked. Reload **http://maker:4001**.

**Step 3 (redo) — the duplicate case, with a safely-equivalent address.** Paste this — it's the same page but with an **uppercased domain, a `www.`, and a trailing slash** (the path is unchanged), then click **Save link**:

```
https://WWW.DEVELOPER.MOZILLA.ORG/en-US/docs/Web/JavaScript/Closures/
```

- It should recognize this as the **same** bookmark and warn you (no duplicate created).
- Now click **"Show the one I already have."** This time it **opens that bookmark in an edit form** (address, title, description, tags, note), not just a highlight.
- Try changing something — e.g. add a tag or a line to the note — and click **Save changes**. Confirm it updates in place.

**Optional, to confirm the path rule:** paste the same address but with the path word in capitals — `.../JavaScript/CLOSURES` — and Save. Because **path capitalization can mean a different page**, this should be treated as a *new, different* bookmark, not a duplicate. (You'll get a second bookmark; you can Edit → it isn't needed, just illustrates the rule.)

Two small assumptions in the edit form to check:
- I put an **"Edit" button on every bookmark card** so editing isn't only reachable via the duplicate path. Reasonable?
- If, while editing, you change the address to one that **already belongs to another bookmark**, it blocks the change (same no-duplicates rule). Right call?

How does editing — and the refined duplicate handling — feel?
